entities.name: Aryl methyl ether substrate
observations: Contains an aryl methoxy group and an unchanged fused diazole-like heteroaromatic core.

entities.name: Phenolic product
observations: Product differs by conversion of Ar-O-CH3 to Ar-OH; core and isopropyl substituent are retained.

entities.name: Aryl ether O-demethylation
observations: The inferred transformation is cleavage of an aryl methyl ether to a phenol, Ar-OCH3 to Ar-OH.
The reaction is a phenol deprotection and does not require oxidation, reduction, coupling, or skeletal rearrangement.

entities.name: Boron tribromide
observations: An exact core-reactant match in ORD-derived records uses BBr3 for the aryl ether cleavage.
BBr3 is the strongest directly supported reagent for this transformation.

entities.name: BBr3 demethylation conditions
observations: Plausible conditions: anhydrous BBr3, typically about 1–3 equivalents, in dry dichloromethane or another dry halogenated solvent; cold addition around -78 to 0 °C followed by warming to room temperature and careful aqueous or alcoholic quench.
Cyclohexene is present in the matched record and is likely an auxiliary scavenger or workup-related reagent rather than a product-incorporated reactant.
